children: As The Leela expands its luxury footprint across high-value destinations, its growth strategy is centred on adding scale while protecting the service standards, pricing power and sense of place that define its proposition

The Leela has spent four decades building a distinctly Indian expression of luxury hospitality. Founded in 1986 with the opening of The Leela Mumbai, the brand has grown from a single hotel into a pure-play luxury hospitality platform spanning palaces, city hotels and resorts. As it enters its next phase of expansion, the challenge is not simply how many hotels The Leela can add, but how it can grow without diluting the exclusivity and service proposition on which the brand has built its reputation.

That makes the perspective of Anuraag Bhatnagar, CEO, The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts, particularly relevant to the owners, developers and investors attending the Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards 2026 at JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity.

The Leela's recent performance demonstrates the strength of its premium positioning. In Q1 FY2027, operating revenue rose 28 per cent year-on-year to Rs 352 crore, while operating EBITDA increased 41 per cent to Rs 143.4 crore. RevPAR grew 17 per cent to Rs 13,982, supported by a 10 per cent increase in ADR to Rs 20,722 and occupancy of 67.5 per cent across its owned domestic hotels, including Coorg.

The company entered FY2027 with 15 operating hotels and 10 hotels in its pipeline, taking the portfolio to 25 properties and 5,257 keys. The pipeline spans destinations including Jaisalmer, Mumbai, Srinagar, Bandhavgarh, Sikkim, Ayodhya, Agra, Ranthambore, Tadoba and Mumbai BKC. These are future additions and are distinct from the 15 hotels already operating.

The expansion is also broadening the definition of where luxury can be created. In July 2026, The Leela launched The Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary, a 71-villa property spread across 76 acres, extending the brand into nature-led and wellness-focused hospitality. During Q1 FY2027, it also signed a concession agreement for a 30-key wildlife resort in Maharashtra's Tadoba Tiger Reserve.

The larger pipeline combines owned and managed assets. The 250-key The Leela Palace BKC is an owned development, while Jaisalmer is a managed project. The Leela Dubai, its first international venture, will comprise 546 keys, including a 361-key hotel, 182 private residences and three villas.
For The Leela, expansion is therefore being pursued alongside continued emphasis on operating performance and service consistency. Its Net Promoter Score stood at 86 in Q1 FY2027.

The next phase of growth will test whether a luxury-only brand can increase its footprint while retaining the scarcity, personalisation and sense of place that allow its hotels to command a premium. For owners and developers, that makes The Leela's expansion model a question not merely of adding keys.
